viewer_sees: the court of examination in a pillared hall: a raised bench of judges in white linen on the left, a scribe writing at their feet; across the right two thirds a long line of more than thirty accused men and women kneeling, wrists bound, heads bowed
the trial papyrus today, under museum glass: a long brown sheet with columns of black hieratic and red-ink headings, its first column broken to fragments, a dim gallery reflection on the glass
the mummy of Ramesses III lying in the dark in its coffin; one thin shaft of light across the dark face and the thick collar of linen wound around the neck

Ramesses III alive, enthroned on the left of his columned hall, crook and flail crossed, facing right; at the right edge a curtained doorway into the women's quarters, where two figures lean together in the shadow

the royal harem as a household, not a pleasure garden: a sunlit walled courtyard with women at upright looms, children with a ball, a steward checking jars against a tally board, and two spear guards at the gate
Tiye in her painted chamber on the right half of the frame, one hand on the shoulder of her son Pentawer, a slim youth; both look toward the left edge
from the shadow of a harem window at the right, Tiye watches across a courtyard: on the left, in sunlight, the king stands at a balcony with his chosen heir, a grown prince, beside him; her face hard

a night meeting around one lamp in Tiye's chamber: the chief of the chamber bows low before Tiye at the right, two royal butlers kneeling beside him → the circle widens: a harem official with his staff of office and an army commander in a leather corselet lean in toward Tiye
at the harem gate at night, the wife of a gate officer passes a folded papyrus letter through the half-open gate to a man waiting outside
in a dark lane of mudbrick houses outside the palace, a man reads the letter aloud to a knot of angry men, faces lit by one torch

in the palace archive, a keeper of rolls hands the overseer of the royal herds a papyrus roll marked with the cartouche of Ramesses III → at the harem gate at night, a covered basket of small wax figures carried past two drowsing guards
MACRO OBJECT — a small wax figure of a man, limbs bound with linen thread, lying across the open magic roll whose margin bears the king's own cartouche; a lamp flame reflected in the wax

EMPTY AFTERMATH — a palace corridor at grey dawn: an overturned oil lamp, a door standing open, a dropped ostrich-feather fan, no people → the plotters dragged bound across the palace court by soldiers, while on a dais at the left the chosen son sits enthroned and watches
a court scribe at a low table writing the first column of the trial papyrus, the king's cartouche at its head in fresh red and black ink

twelve judges standing in a row before an empty throne on which lie the king's crook and flail, while a herald reads the commission → the dead Ramesses III walking among a line of earlier kings into the hall of the gods, toward a colossal enthroned Osiris and Amun-Ra with tall plumes, light pouring from them
the gilded coffin face of Ramesses III, eyes painted wide open, in the darkness of his tomb, lit by one torch, as if listening

MACRO OBJECT — a scribe's reed brush writing a new name in red ink into the record → a kneeling royal butler under a blazing sun disc, and beside him a kneeling archer captain, both heads bowed → a human-headed ba bird lifting away from an oval name-ring being chiselled blank on a stone
in the court of examination, guards lead twenty-two bound condemned out through a bright doorway at the right, while six men sit alone on the floor of the emptied hall below the empty judges' bench
Prince Pentawer brought before three seated butlers acting as judges, standing straight in white linen with bound wrists, facing left
close on Pentawer's face in lamplight, half in shadow, eyes lowered — a face without its own name
SILHOUETTE — the prince alone in a small shut room, seated on a bench, a black silhouette against a lamplit wall; no body, no weapon

two well-fed judges in fine pleated robes, wrists now bound, standing before a new tribunal → the beer-hall: at night in a judge's house, the two judges reclining among harem women and an army commander, beer jars, a harpist, lamps, laughter
the two judges sitting against a mudbrick wall, the middles of their faces bound in linen over nose and ears, heads bowed; one has turned toward a dark doorway
SILHOUETTE — Tiye as a dark figure in a doorway at the end of a long empty corridor, light behind her, turned away
two Egyptologists of the 1890s arguing across a desk piled with books, a facsimile of the papyrus spread between them and a photograph of the mummy's face pinned to the wall

1881, the hidden royal tomb: a narrow rock-cut corridor crammed with stacked coffins, workmen with candles hauling one coffin toward the shaft → close on the mummy's neck: a thick collar of layered brown linen, tight under the chin
2012, a CT room: the mummy of Ramesses III on the scanner table, half inside the white ring of the gantry; two researchers at the console screens

PROCESS / CUTAWAY — the CT slice on the monitor: a grey section of the neck where, under the pale ring of linen, a black gap cuts straight back through the windpipe to the white bones of the spine; a researcher's fingertip traces it
three thousand years earlier, in the embalming tent: an embalmer in a jackal mask presses a small blue Eye of Horus amulet into the king's throat while another winds linen around the neck
the king's coffin dragged on a sledge into the dark mouth of his tomb, mourners with raised arms → priests lowering the blue crown onto the head of the chosen son on the throne
back in the 1881 royal cache: set apart from the painted royal coffins, one plain undecorated coffin with its lid shifted aside, a wrapped body inside, a candle held over it
the young man's head and shoulders, wrapped in a rough goatskin, the face contorted, mouth wide open as if screaming
1886: a pen writing a single large letter E on a paper tag tied with string to the plain coffin

two mummies on lab tables side by side, the king on the left and the young man on the right, profiles turned toward each other, a researcher holding a sample tube up between them → Pentawer alive again in the lamplit court, looking toward the left
night in Cairo: a line of golden carriages shaped like ancient boats rolling toward the right past the obelisk in Tahrir Square, crowds and lights along the road
two golden carriages close: the leading one at the right carries the cartouche of Ramesses III on its side; directly behind it at the left rolls the carriage of his son

the plain coffin of the young man alone in a dark museum storeroom, a high window at the left lit gold by the parade passing outside → the screaming face in a glass case, a small blank-looking label card at its lower edge
EMPTY AFTERMATH — an oval name-ring carved in stone, its inside chiselled empty, sand drifting into it → END CARD: poster of the whole story with title and SUBSCRIBE
